2012_035_050112regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of May 1, 2012, in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. It covers recognition of Outstanding Support Staff Award winner Linda Tackett, the 2011-2012 retirees, National Teacher Appreciation Week (May 7-11, 2012), the April 17, 2012 minutes, curriculum reports on social studies textbooks for grades 6-12 and K-5 English language arts materials, and a slate of policy readings. The most consequential action is the appointment of Joseph Duda as Principal of Larson Middle School on a two-year probationary administrative contract effective July 1, 2012.
2012_035_050112regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, May 1, 2012, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August.

**Recognition**
Linda Tackett, Health Care Aide at Baker Middle School, was named recipient of the 2011-2012 Outstanding Support Staff Award; the resolution notes she started as a Health Care Aide in March of 2001. The award is administered with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association (TESA) and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA). The packet lists Troy School District employees retiring at the end of the 2011-2012 school year, including Denny Seppanen, Principal of Larson Middle School (43 years), Gary Wood, Principal of Costello Elementary School (39 years), Sheryl Fragomeni, Reading Specialist at Leonard Elementary (40 years), Lori Rekucki, 3rd grade teacher at Bemis (39 years), and Pauline Walker, English teacher at Athens High School (39 years). Jasen Witt reads each name; Board President Nancy Philippart presents each retiree with a clock. A resolution supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 7-11, 2012.

**Consent agenda**
Approval of the minutes of the April 17, 2012 Board of Education meeting, which are reproduced in full.

**Personnel**
Recommendation to appoint Mr. Joseph Duda as Principal, Larson Middle School, effective July 1, 2012, on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure. Duda joined Troy in June of 1999 as an Athens High School science teacher and became Assistant Principal in December of 2006; degrees are a Bachelor of Science in Education from Central Michigan University (1998), a Master of Education in Science Curriculum from Wayne State University (2002), and an Education Specialist degree in School Administration from Oakland University (2004).

**Curriculum reports** (both presented by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment)

| Report | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Social Studies grades 6-12 textbook adoption | Process began August 31, 2011; vendor presentations November 3, 2011 (four vendors) and February 23, 2012 (three vendors); continued evaluation November 3 - February 22, 2012 |
| English Language Arts K-5 material adoption | Recommends Houghton Mifflin Harcourt (HMH) materials for grades K-5 in July 2012, following HMH Literature for grades 9-12 in July 2010 and grades 6-8 in July 2011 |

ELA rollout includes a half-day with author Shane Templeton for all elementary teachers in May, a set of 15 mentor texts plus online access for each teacher in fall of 2012, professional development on August 29, 2012 and in September of 2012, and at least two additional half-days during 2012-2013.

**Other business**
Scheduling of a Special Board of Education Meeting on Tuesday, May 15, 2012, at the Administrative Building for Business items and adoption of the Oakland Schools Biennial Election resolution. First reading of revisions to Board Policies B-1302 Agendas for Regular Meetings, G-1401 Political Activities, K-1303 Commercial Advertising, K-1401 Solicitations on School Property, and of new Policies C-1501 E-mail Retention and J-2012 Anti-Bullying. Second reading and consideration of revisions to B-1209 Board Member Abstention from Voting and K-1301 Distribution of Materials to Students, first read on April 17, 2012.

Board packet and agenda for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held May 1, 2012, at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District address is 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, telephone 248.823.4000, website www.troy.k12.mi.us. Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August, and viewable at www.troy.k12.mi.us/tsdnews/video.htm. Agenda order: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communications (agenda items); General-Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Adjournment.

CONSENT AGENDA. Approval of the minutes of the April 17, 2012 Board of Education meeting, reproduced in the packet. Those minutes record President Philippart calling the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. at the Services Building, with board members Edmunds, Hauff, Fleming, Miletti, Schmidt, and Underwood present, along with Superintendent Fowler; administrators Brzezinski, Canfield, Colligan, Jansen, Keeling, MacDonald, Machesky, Mull, Rajter, and Witt; and approximately 70 members of the audience. Philippart welcomed student representatives Asja Kepes, a junior representing International Academy-East, and Marcarius Coakley, a senior representing Niles Community High School. The Board recognized the Facilities Study Team - Rahmat Awan, Gregory Bryen, David Cole, Scott Courtney, Adeyinka Dawodu, Jamie Douglas, Waqar Hashim, Laurie Huber, Dale Jerome, Lynda Keough, Bernard Lourim, John Mayernik, Denise Murray, Heather Plastow, Kim Rosseter, Nehal Shah, Pete van der Harst, and Pete Ziegenfelder - with liaisons Mike Zinn and Stu Redpath; each member received a plaque. Teacher of the Year nominees were Debbie Brorson (Schroeder), Mark Cavataio (Wass), Pamela Mulligan (Hill), Gretchen Vogelei (Martell), Susan Pickering (Smith), and Glenn Rexer (Smith); Cavataio was selected elementary Teacher of the Year and Pickering the middle school and District overall Teacher of the Year. Mike Cianciolo, president of the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, reported the Foundation funded a total of 110 separate grants submitted by teachers, parents and student groups, each recipient awarded a $500 grant, with recipients spanning Troy Union, Morse, Leonard, Wattles, Hill, GSRP, Schroeder, Costello, Martell, Wass, Bemis, Barnard, Hamilton, Building Blocks, Baker, Smith, Larson, Boulan, Troy High, Athens, Niles Center, Troy Center for Transition and district departments. He announced the Dr. Janet Jopke Memorial Fun Walk on Saturday, May 19th and the Tony Spagnola Invitational Golf Outing on June 22nd at Sanctuary Lake Golf Course, plus a Charity Poker fundraiser. Resolution 12-029 approved the March 20, 2012 meeting minutes, the March 20, 2012 workshop minutes, and the Treasurer's Report for February and March 2012 (Ayes 7, Nays 0), moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming. Jasen Witt, assistant superintendent for Human Resources, presented a District Health Insurance Update covering changes from collective bargaining and legislation, High Deductible Health Plans (HDHP) with Health Savings Accounts (HSA), and new plan options for administrative, non-rep and TESPA groups, noting the TESA and TEA collective bargaining agreements expire on June 30, 2013. Rich Machesky, assistant superintendent for secondary instruction, presented District goals in literacy, math, science and social studies, referencing NCA external review, annual peer review, the Student Learning Showcase, Student Artifact Review and Vision 2013; he noted the District is limited by seats offered through Oakland Schools for the 24 teachers to be trained in MI Class literacy for social studies, and that 46 states agreed to adopt the Common Core State Standards with assessments provided in the spring of 2015. Anne Mull presented 2011-2012 MEAP results for grades 3-9 in math, reading, science and social studies, addressing changed cut scores and 7-year trends. Steve Dunneback addressed the Board on small class sizes, citing research on K-3 classrooms with fewer than 20 students. First readings were held on B-1209 Board Member Abstentions from Voting (read by Mr. Miletti) and K-1301 Distribution of Materials to Students (read by Mrs. Fleming). Resolution 12-030, moved by Ms. Underwood and supported by Mr. Miletti, approved changes to Board policy B-1401 Minutes and adopted new policy I-1701 Opting Out of Video Presentations (Ayes 7, Nays 0), after readings by Mrs. Edmunds and Mr. Schmidt. Student representatives reported: Maggie Steele (Troy High) on Activist Week and online prom tickets; Lisa Lavelanet (Athens, in Jonny Dowdall's place) that composite ACT scores for juniors increased by 1.4 since last year, seven Model UN awards at Michigan State, the MASC/MATIS Award of Excellence, and over $35,000 raised in February for "I've Got Your Back," with the Ethnic Fair April 25th at 5:00 p.m. and Athens' Got Talent April 27th at 7:00 p.m.; Asja Kepes on IA-East's first graduating class and IB exams; and Marcarius Coakley on Niles Community High School. Mr. Hauff noted Troy High students Dorothy Chen and Sara Ma won the YouTube Space Lab and were congratulated by Senator Carl Levin. Mr. Miletti noted Plante & Moran and Clark Hill as golf outing sponsors (www.troyfoudation.org). Dr. Fowler announced selection as one of the 2012 Best Communities for Music Education. Resolution 12-031, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Hauff, took the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) to discuss negotiations; roll call was Philippart, Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti all Yes, motion carried 7-0. Closed session began at 9:30 p.m., the meeting reconvened at 9:35 p.m., and adjourned at 10:40 p.m. Minutes submitted by Todd Miletti, Secretary.

PERSONNEL (6.A.). Recommendation to appoint Mr. Joseph Duda as Principal, Larson Middle School. Duda came to Troy in June of 1999 as a science teacher at Athens High School and moved into Assistant Principal in December of 2006; during his 13 years at Athens he co-chaired a school improvement team and served on the NCA school improvement committee and the Teacher Evaluation Committee (TEAM), participated in and contributed to the T.A.L.L. program, and served as Administrative Liaison for Secondary Mathematics and Science. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Education from Central Michigan University (1998), a Master of Education in Science Curriculum from Wayne State University (2002), and an Education Specialist degree in School Administration from Oakland University (2004). The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2012.

CURRICULUM (7.A.). Report on the Social Studies Grades 6-12 Textbook Adoption, presented by Anne Mull, Director of Instruction and Assessment. Work began August 31, 2011 with survey needs assessment and data results, an overview of Common Core literacy standards, and selection of social studies teachers. Timeline: November 3, 2011 presentations by four vendors; November 3 - February 22, 2012 continued evaluation; February 23, 2012 presentations by three vendors; teachers then selected materials. Current and proposed course sequences run from grade 6 geography through grade 12 World History and Geography 2, with grade 7 Ancient Civilizations, grade 8 Integrated U.S. History through Reconstruction, grade 9 Government/World History and Geo. 1, grade 10 American History, and grade 11 Economics and Government or Economics and World His. & Geo 1. Evaluation criteria included reading level, alignment to standards, differentiation, NIMAS compliance for special education, test bank quality, SmartBoard and internet resources, and practice activities in digital and hard copy. Instructional frameworks cited include Understanding by Design (Grant Wiggins and Jay McTighe), Nonlinguistic Representation (Robert Marzano), Multiple Intelligences (Howard Gardner), Cooperative Interaction (Elizabeth Cohen), and Spiral Curriculum (Jerome Bruner). Featured materials include chapter-level videos, podcasts for essential questions, downloadable eReader files, Essential Question Journals, Economics and You, How the Economy Works, Visual Glossary, Action Graphs, Quick Study Guides, a Personal Finance handbook, and American Government on the Go audio and video.

CURRICULUM (7.B.). Report on English Language Arts Material Adoption, Grades K-5, also presented by Anne Mull. Prior purchases were Houghton Mifflin Harcourt (HMH) Literature for grades 9-12 in July 2010 and grades 6-8 in July 2011; the recommendation is purchase of HMH materials for grades K-5 in July 2012. New materials will supplement, not supplant, existing resources and align to all strands of the English Common Core Standards - reading, writing, listening, speaking, viewing, language (grammar), and technology. Rollout begins in spring with professional development in word study; author and researcher Shane Templeton will spend a half-day with all elementary teachers in May, and teachers receive the HMH Word Study Teacher Guide referencing HMH Journeys mentor text. In fall of 2012, with approval, each teacher receives a set of 15 mentor texts and online access. On August 29, 2012 teachers receive professional development in using the materials in the workshop model; in September of 2012 each elementary teacher receives training in the workshop model and differentiation including for English language learners; at least two additional half-days are scheduled during the 2012-2013 school year. Components listed include the Comprehensive Language and Literacy Guide: A Readers Workshop Approach, Word Study Guide, Decodable Readers, Big Books, Online Leveled Readers, Student eBook, Language Support Cards for English Language Learners, Interactive Smart Board Lessons, Focus Wall Posters, online Comprehensive Screening/Diagnostic Assessment for grades 2-5, Vocabulary Readers, Write-In Readers for Intervention, WriteSmart CD-ROM, ExamView Assessment on CD-ROM, Teacher One-Stop Planner CD-ROM, and Interactive Simulations by Destination Reading (2013-2014). Guided reading support is based on Irene Fountas principles. A Troy Balanced Literacy diagram lays out Reader's Workshop, Word Study, and Writer's Workshop, with Big Books for grades K-1, Decodable Readers for grades K-2, and Trade Novels for grades 3-6.

OTHER (10.A.). Consideration of a resolution to schedule a Special Board of Education Meeting on Tuesday, May 15, 2012, at the Administrative Building prior to the Board Workshop, for Business items and adoption of the Oakland Schools Biennial Election resolution.

OTHER (10.B.). First reading of revisions to Board Policies B-1302 Agendas for Regular Meetings, G-1401 Political Activities, K-1303 Commercial Advertising, K-1401 Solicitations on School Property, and new Board Policies C-1501 E-mail Retention and J-2012 Anti-Bullying, all reviewed by the Board's attorney for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act, and the Revised School Code; each Board member reads a policy round-robin. B-1302 (series B-1300) provides that the agenda is prepared by the superintendent and Board president, delivered to members five calendar days preceding the meeting, posted at the Administrative Center four calendar days preceding the meeting with the agenda and board packet made available on the district website the day of but prior to the meeting, delivered at least twenty-four hours before special meetings, and that adding or deleting an item requires a motion seconded and approved by a vote of at least four members; revised January 16, 1979, March 17, 1998, and June 19, 2007. G-1401 Political Activities (series G-1400) recognizes employees' right to campaign and hold office while barring campaigning during school hours, use of district supplies or equipment, involvement of students, and display of political material on district property except on personal vehicles parked there; it requires complete neutrality by all school personnel including contracted personnel and restricts use of District resources, technology including District e-mail, and student/parent contact information absent written consent of the superintendent or designee; adopted January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998. K-1303 Political and/or Commercial Advertising by District Employees (series K-1300) carries parallel prohibitions plus a commercial-purpose restriction; adopted May 3, 1976, revised January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998, and April 20, 2010. K-1401 Solicitations (series K-1400) prohibits solicitations on school property, including product, article, service or political solicitations, unless approved by the superintendent or designee or involving an isolated, private, person-to-person legal transaction; adopted April 19, 1976, revised January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998, and March 23, 2012. New policy C-1501 E-mail Retention (series C-1500) applies to all users except students, defining User to include employees, officers, temporary employees, interns, vendors, consultants, contractors, authorized agents and volunteers; it requires mailbox management under Technology Resource Center (TRC) size limits, automatic deletion by TRC of e-mail and note items more than one year in age unless retained pursuant to law, court order, direction of the Superintendent, the Board's records policy K-1002, or the Records Retention and Disposal Schedule of Michigan Public Schools (Educational Bulletin #522); backups of the District e-mail system are kept only two business days; litigation holds suspend destruction until TRC is directed otherwise by the Superintendent's Office; electronic calendars and task items are available for two years; and beginning July 1, 2012 the District e-mail system will use an archive system retaining user messages for one year, with automatic destruction of archived messages more than one year old except when quarantined for litigation. New policy J-2012 Anti-Bullying (series J-2000) prohibits bullying at school, defines bullying as any written, verbal, or physical act or electronic communication intended or reasonably known to be likely to harm students by substantially interfering with educational opportunities, placing a student in reasonable fear of physical harm or causing substantial emotional distress, having a substantial detrimental effect on physical or mental health, or causing substantial disruption; prohibits retaliation and false accusation; requires prompt reporting to the principal or designee, prompt and thorough investigation by the building principal or designee, notification to the parent/guardian of both victim and perpetrator, and at least annual reporting of verified incidents and consequences to the Board of Education; designates the superintendent as Responsible School Official; requires annual circulation, conspicuous posting, annual discussion with students, and inclusion in handbooks; and defines "at school" and adopts the definitions of "Telecommunications Access Device" and "Telecommunications Service Provider" from Section 219a of the Michigan Penal Code, 1931 PA 328, MCL 750.219a.

OTHER (10.C.). Second reading and consideration of revisions to Board Policy B-1209 Board Member Abstention from Voting and K-1301 Distribution of Materials to Students, first read at the April 17, 2012 meeting. B-1209 (series B-1200) as revised provides that a member shall abstain from voting affirmatively or negatively if a direct or indirect financial conflict of interest exists, if there is an appearance of a direct or indirect conflict of interest, or if abstention is explicitly required by the Board's by-laws or applicable law, with the nature of the conflict recorded in the minutes and abstention for any other reason not permitted; adopted April 8, 1975, revised June 7, 1977 and January 16, 1979. K-1301 requires individuals or organizations not representing students, teachers, administrators, or school-sponsored organizations to obtain prior approval of the superintendent or designee before distributing handwritten, duplicated or printed materials or lapel pins, stickers, tags or similar items to students or to parents through students, while preserving advertising in student publications published by student organizations; adopted April 19, 1976, revised January 16, 1979 and April 21, 1998.
